transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. whenever you're ready, tell me your dream however it comes back to you.
hey! the part that stuck with me most was the house—it was this ordinary looking place from outside but then inside it was way bigger, like there was a whole little village in there

a whole little village inside an ordinary house. that's the kind of thing that stays with you.

what was the first thing you noticed once you were inside?
there was this cobblestone street, like something from europe, and a guy kind of like a pied piper with curly hair, juggling and stuff

a village with its own cobblestone street and a pied piper type, right there inside the house.

did he seem to notice you, or was he off in his own world?
i don't really remember if he noticed me, i think i just went past him

just passing through. makes sense, the man's busy juggling.

where did you end up after that?
i went up the back stairs—there were two sets, so right when i got to the top i went straight down the other side. then there was a short empty hallway that turned a corner

those two sets back to back, like a tiny bridge between parts of the house.

what was around that corner?
a tiny room with a young woman in it. she had shoulder-length blonde hair in a pageboy, and she was cooking at a stove that almost filled the room

she had her own tucked-away spot, cooking in a room the stove nearly swallowed.

did you talk to her, or just watch for a second?
she was nice to me, i'm pretty sure we talked a little, but i don't remember what about

that's okay, conversations in dreams drift like that. what mattered was that she was kind.

where'd you go next?
i was outside waiting for my aunt, and she pulled up in a little round convertible

a little round convertible. something about the shape of it feels like it belongs to the same dream as that house.

can you picture the car at all—like what color it was, or how she looked when she pulled up?
i don't remember the color, just that it was small and round. i don't really remember how she looked in that moment either

that's okay. some things in dreams are more of a feeling than a picture.

what happened after she picked you up?
we drove a little, crossed a little bridge over a creek, then doubled back and she dropped me off at the house again

back at the house, after that little loop over the creek. feels like the house was the real center of everything.

how did it feel to be back there?
i ended up inside, sitting with a couple of people, playing with a string of blue balloons—that part was kind of chill

a chill kind of ending, blue balloons and a couple of people.

did you know the people you were sitting with?
i don't remember who they were

just company, then. that can be enough.

you've told me a lot about what happened. i'm curious now—were you in the dream as yourself, just moving through it, or did it feel different from that?
i don't fully remember, but i think i was just me moving through it

got it. just you, drifting through a house full of impossible rooms and old streets.

how did the spaces feel while you were in them—cozy, open, strange, a mix?
a mix, i guess. the village felt weirdly open, but the little room with the stove was super cramped and cozy

that contrast is neat—the village sprawling inside a house, then that little hot kitchen, almost too small for both of you.

did the dream feel bright, dim, warm, or something else?
i think it felt kind of bright and warm, especially the village part

bright and warm. i can almost see it, the cobblestones lit up like afternoon.

was there any sound in the dream—music, the juggler, the stove, voices?
i don't really remember many sounds, just maybe general noise from the village, like people around

a low hum of village life, but nothing specific. that still gives it atmosphere.

the house, the spaces, the way it stitched together?
i think it fits the dream pretty well, honestly

good. thanks for walking me through it.

were you already in the house, or did something lead you there?
i'm not really sure how i got there, i just remember being inside at the start

some dreams are like that—no entrance, just already there.

you were sitting with the balloons, was that the last thing you remember?
yeah, that's where my memory ends

you were already inside an ordinary-looking house that turned out to be huge inside, with a whole little village. there was a cobblestone street like in europe, and a curly-haired guy kind of like a pied piper juggling, but you just passed him. you went up some back stairs, down another set right away, through a short empty hallway around a corner, and came to a tiny room where a young woman with a pageboy was cooking at a stove that almost filled the room. she was nice and you talked a little. then you were outside waiting for your aunt, who pulled up in a little round convertible. you drove a bit, crossed a bridge over a creek, doubled back, and she dropped you off at the house again. you ended up inside sitting with a couple of people, playing with a string of blue balloons, and it was chill. the village felt open, the little room cramped and cozy, and the whole dream felt bright and warm, with just a general village noise and nothing specific.

does that sound right, or did i miss anything?
that's pretty much it, yeah. the only thing is i don't remember there being much sound, not even sure about the general village noise—but if there was, it was nothing specific

got it, no real sound then—just a quiet dream.

thanks for going through it with me.
yeah, thanks for asking about it! it was fun trying to piece it back together😊

i enjoyed hearing it too.

any chance you'd like to see it drawn? i can help turn it into a picture.
oh yeah, that would be really cool!

sure, we can do that.

there are a few ways it could be drawn. one is warm and loose, like ink and wash where the line wanders a little, as if it's drawn from memory. another is bright and storybook-like, with solid, friendly shapes and a simple, homemade feel. there's also a light pencil sketch with touches of color, the line searching and careful, then left alone. and a fourth keeps the edges sharp and the colors as they were, like a memory kept in bright detail. which of those feels closest to your dream, or would you describe your own way?
hmm, i think the first one, warm and loose like it's drawn from memory, feels closest to the dream

warm and loose it is. i'll start with you.

and since you're in it too, i'd like to draw you in there. would you like me to draw you as you are—maybe tell me a little about how you look—or however i imagine you?
how you imagine me is fine, i don’t remember how i looked in the dream anyway

i'm sketching you and the pied piper and the young woman and the aunt and the couple of people and the ordinary house exterior and the village street and the back stairs and the short hallway and the tiny room and the waiting spot and the road and bridge and the balloon room and the little round convertible and the string of blue balloons now.

everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
oh wow, that's so cool! the vibe feels right with the warm loose style. let me look through them😊
take your time, i'll be here. whenever you're ready, tell me if anything looks off or feels right to you.
the village street and cobblestones look really close, and the tiny room with the big stove fits—cramped and cozy. the aunt's little round convertible is basically what i pictured

i'm so glad those feel right—the street, the cramped cozy room, the little round convertible.

take your time with the rest whenever they show up.

the back stairs and the second set going down feel right too, and i like the balloon room—it has that chill feeling. the ordinary house outside is good, it looks tiny compared to everything inside, same as in the dream

the house looking tiny outside and huge inside is exactly the kind of dream logic i love. so glad the street, the room, the car, the stairs, and the balloons all feel right to you.

the rest are still being sketched, they'll appear on the right in a bit.
the pied piper guy is good too—curly hair and all. he looks busy, like i'd just pass him without stopping

he looks busy, like you'd just pass him without stopping. that's exactly the feeling.

the rest are still being sketched, they'll appear on the right soon.
the waiting spot feels right, like outside the house but not too far. and the road and bridge with the creek look good—it's a little quiet scene, like we just crossed and came back
the waiting spot and the road and bridge feeling right—that little quiet loop over the creek, crossing and coming back. i'm glad. the rest are still being sketched, they'll appear on the right soon.
the young woman in the tiny room is good too—pageboy hair and the stove almost filling the room. she looks kind, like she was nice to me
the young woman with the pageboy hair and the stove filling the room—i'm glad she looks kind, like she was nice to you. the rest are still being sketched, they'll appear on the right soon.
the short hallway turning the corner is right, empty like i remember. and my aunt in the convertible fits—just a small round car, nothing too fancy
the empty hallway and the small round car, both just right. i'm glad they match what you remember.
